source: Ministry of Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation extension leaflet, "ដំណាំសណ្តែកកួរ" [Yard-long bean/cowpea cultivation], 2013
text:
This 2013 extension leaflet on yard-long bean/cowpea (សណ្តែកកួរ) gives a fertilizer-timing schedule tied to days after planting — applications at day 0 (basal), and follow-up top-dressings at days 3, 5, 7, 10, and 14 after planting, each with a specific fertilizer type and rate, reflecting the crop's fast early growth and need for frequent light feeding rather than one or two large doses.

A pest note flags caterpillar/worm damage to flowers (described as a worm that feeds on the flower buds, reducing pod set) as a problem to watch for during the flowering stage, with control recommended through timely inspection and targeted insecticide application when infestation is found rather than routine spraying.

Harvest guidance recommends picking pods while still young and tender for best eating/market quality, with repeated harvesting over the crop's extended flowering-and-fruiting period as is typical for this vegetable-type legume (unlike grain/pulse beans, yard-long bean is harvested green and repeatedly rather than once at dry maturity).
